districts.reasoning: Banadir is a structurally heterogeneous urban district hosting Somalia's largest IDP population (~250-500k across 2017-21). Although urban diversified livelihoods support a lower host-community SAM burden, the persistent IDP settlements have shown Critical SAM (>=4%) across multiple FSNAU surveys, sustaining elevated structural gamma. CMAM coverage and survey infrastructure are the country's most consistent, lowering omega; survey quality is the highest in the country.

Afgooye corridor is a structurally riverine/agropastoral district hosting one of the largest IDP corridors in Somalia. Recurrent Shabelle flooding, mixed AS/government control fluctuating along main supply routes, and chronic IDP nutritional vulnerability elevate gamma; partial AS pressure on rural areas raises omega but Afgooye town is regularly surveyed.

Marka district mixes Lower Shabelle riverine (SO13) and rainfed agropastoral (SO16) zones. Persistent AS presence in rural sub-districts across 2017-21 chronically limited humanitarian access; main town surveyed irregularly. Structural gamma is elevated by agricultural insecurity; omega is elevated by access constraints.

Riverine pump-irrigation district structurally vulnerable to Shabelle flooding and chronic AS-related access restrictions during 2017-21. Despite agricultural potential, chronic insecurity and recurrent flooding sustain elevated gamma; omega elevated by intermittent survey access.

Small Lower Shabelle district that was structurally outside government control across most of 2017-21, severely limiting CMAM and survey access. Chronically inaccessible districts have very high omega; structural gamma is high given agropastoral fragility and lack of programme presence.

Lower Shabelle district persistently under AS influence during 2017-21 with very limited humanitarian penetration. Structural agropastoral/riverine vulnerability with absent CMAM produces high gamma, low p (chronic, untreated SAM), and high omega.

Coastal Lower Shabelle district with mixed fishing, agropastoral and riverine livelihoods. Coastal access provided some structural diet diversification, mitigating gamma; AS presence in rural hinterland generated intermittent access constraints raising omega.

Lower Shabelle agropastoral district with chronic AS-related access constraints in rural areas, structurally limiting CMAM coverage. Gamma elevated by agricultural insecurity; omega elevated by sparse survey coverage.

Middle Shabelle riverine/agropastoral district historically reaching famine-level acute malnutrition (2011) and structurally fragile thereafter. Mixed IDP hosting from Mogadishu outflows and chronic flooding; partially government-controlled with moderate CMAM access.

Middle Shabelle coastal-agropastoral district with chronic AS pressure in rural areas. Historically among famine-classified zones (2011) and structurally vulnerable; survey frequency below average raises omega.

Middle Shabelle regional capital, riverine/agropastoral, structurally exposed to recurrent Shabelle flooding. Town-level CMAM access is moderate; rural AS presence raises omega. Some IDP hosting from Lower Shabelle and rural displacement.

Adan Yabaal was under AS control for ~12 years until late 2022, so across the entire 2017-21 study period it was structurally inaccessible to humanitarian and survey actors. Very high omega (no reliable surveys), structurally high gamma (no CMAM), and low p (no recovery pathway).
Middle Shabelle/Hiraan riverine district structurally exposed to flooding and chronic AS rural pressure. Limited CMAM scale; sparse survey coverage raises omega.

Belet Weyne is the Hiraan regional capital with riverine and agropastoral hinterland; structurally exposed to recurrent flooding and shows persistent Critical/Serious GAM in FSNAU surveys. Town has reliable CMAM and surveys; rural AS pressure elevates omega moderately.

Bulo Burto remained substantially under AS control across 2017-21, structurally limiting CMAM and survey access. Riverine/agropastoral fragility with chronic insecurity yields high gamma and very high omega; low p reflects absence of treatment pathway.

Galmudug administrative capital in Central Agropastoral Cowpea Belt (SO10). Structurally diversified agropastoral economy; town-level IDP settlements have shown elevated GAM across surveys but generally lower than southern agropastoral. Reliable surveys and moderate CMAM access.
Central Agropastoral Cowpea Belt district with relatively stable government access. Moderate structural risk; consistent FSNAU monitoring and CMAM presence.

Galgaduud district within the Central Agropastoral Cowpea Belt (SO10), structurally diversified between cowpea cultivation and pastoral livelihoods. Largely Galmudug-administered with stable rural access; moderate CMAM and survey coverage. Structural vulnerability moderate.
Ceel Buur was under AS control across 2017-21 (recovered later), structurally inaccessible to CMAM and surveys. High gamma, very high omega, low p reflect chronic untreated SAM.
Ceel Dheere remained under AS control for most of 2017-21, structurally inaccessible. Mixed agropastoral and coastal Deeh livelihoods with no consistent CMAM presence. High omega and gamma, low p.

Coastal Deeh pastoral/fishing district; structurally fragile and chronically AS-affected during 2017-21. Coastal Deeh (SO08) has shown Critical SAM in past surveys; absence of CMAM access yields very high omega.

Gaalkacyo is a major IDP-hosting urban centre split between Puntland and Galmudug, with Galkayo IDPs sustaining Serious-to-Critical GAM levels across FSNAU surveys for years. Reliable surveys lower omega; structural IDP burden raises gamma; CMAM access strong.
Coastal Deeh (SO08) pastoral/fishing district with structurally chronic vulnerability and intermittent AS presence. Sparse survey access raises omega; absence of consistent CMAM yields modest p.

Mudug pastoral district along the Ethiopian border with Hawd/Addun pastoral livelihoods. Government-controlled with moderate CMAM access; structural pastoral vulnerability but no chronic AS isolation.

Addun Pastoral (SO09) district in Mudug; structural pastoral vulnerability moderated by Puntland administrative stability. Consistent moderate CMAM access; livelihood homogeneity supports survey reliability.

Baidoa is the largest IDP hub outside Mogadishu (sites grew from ~70 in 2017 to 435 in 2019) and the heart of Bay agropastoral SO12, the historically highest-SAM zone in Somalia (famine 2011, Critical SAM repeatedly). Structurally very high gamma; surveys frequent (low omega); CMAM scaled up but demand always exceeds supply.
Baidoa-Buur Hakaba livelihood zone has shown SAM ~4.9% in recent assessments. Structurally high gamma; rural AS presence intermittently restricted access raising omega; partial CMAM coverage.

Diinsoor (Bay) was substantially AS-controlled across 2017-21, structurally inaccessible for most of the period. Bay agropastoral fragility plus no CMAM yields very high gamma and omega; low p reflects chronic untreated SAM.
Bay agropastoral district structurally AS-affected during 2017-21. Chronic SO12 vulnerability with absent CMAM and irregular surveys: high gamma, very high omega.

Bakool regional capital, government-held but surrounded by AS rural areas, structurally limiting supply lines. Bakool agropastoral/pastoral has shown Critical SAM repeatedly. Town-level CMAM partial; rural surveys very irregular.

Bakool district persistently AS-controlled throughout 2017-21, structurally inaccessible. Mixed Southern Inland Pastoral/agropastoral; absence of CMAM and surveys yields very high omega and gamma, low p.

Bakool agropastoral district under chronic AS pressure during 2017-21 with structurally limited humanitarian access. SO12 baseline plus inaccessibility yields very high gamma and omega; chronic untreated SAM lowers p.
Bakool agropastoral district structurally AS-affected and remote. SO12 chronic vulnerability with no consistent CMAM or survey access yields high gamma, very high omega.
Small Bakool district structurally inaccessible during most of 2017-21 due to AS control. SO12 baseline plus isolation yields very high gamma and omega.

Gedo regional capital; North/South Gedo agropastoral and pastoral consistently among highest-SAM zones (>4% SAM in multiple FSNAU surveys). Town-level partial CMAM; rural AS presence raises omega; structural gamma very high.
Gedo riverine/agropastoral district with the Doolow IDP corridor. Sustained Critical SAM in IDP settlements; town has moderate CMAM access. Structural IDP burden elevates gamma; mixed surveys.

Doolow hosts one of Somalia's largest sustained IDP settlements with persistent Critical SAM (~5% SAM repeatedly). Border-crossing humanitarian access supports CMAM and frequent surveys, lowering omega; structural IDP burden keeps gamma very high.
Gedo border district with cross-border humanitarian access supporting CMAM. Structural agropastoral vulnerability with elevated baseline; surveys moderately frequent.
Gedo border district with chronic AS pressure intermittently restricting access. SO12 structural vulnerability; intermittent CMAM and irregular surveys raise omega.

Baardheere remained under AS control for most of 2017-21, structurally inaccessible. Gedo agropastoral baseline already among highest in Somalia; absence of CMAM and surveys yields very high gamma and omega, low p.
Middle Juba regional capital under AS control throughout 2017-21, structurally inaccessible. Riverine/cattle pastoral mix; no CMAM, no surveys. Very high gamma and omega, low p.
Middle Juba riverine district under AS control across 2017-21, structurally inaccessible. SO13 vulnerability plus no CMAM yields very high gamma and omega.
Middle Juba riverine district under AS control during 2017-21. Structural Shabelle/Juba flood vulnerability plus no humanitarian access yields very high gamma and omega.

Kismayo is a major IDP-hosting port city with Jubaland administrative presence and relatively low overall poverty (lowest among major cities per SHFS 2017-18). Reliable CMAM and survey infrastructure; IDP settlements show Serious GAM. Lower structural gamma than Bay/Banadir IDP, lower omega.
Lower Juba pastoral/cattle district with chronic AS rural pressure. Juba cattle pastoral consistently noted as area of high concern; intermittent CMAM and surveys raise omega.
Remote Lower Juba district under chronic AS influence and structurally hard to reach. Pastoral/coastal mix; near-absent humanitarian programming yields high gamma and very high omega.
Lower Juba riverine district with persistent AS pressure restricting rural access. Structural Juba flooding vulnerability and irregular surveys raise omega.

Major Puntland port city with substantial IDP settlements; relatively diversified urban economy and consistent Puntland administrative access support CMAM and frequent surveys. IDP nutritional vulnerability raises gamma somewhat; overall structural risk moderate.

East Golis Frankincense, Goats and Fishing zone (SO07); structurally diversified income (frankincense + livestock + fishing) supports relatively low chronic vulnerability. Remote location reduces survey frequency raising omega.
East Golis (SO07) Bari district with diversified frankincense/pastoral/fishing economy. Remote interior reduces survey coverage; otherwise relatively stable.
Coastal Bari district within East Golis SO07; livelihood diversification through fishing and frankincense moderates structural risk. Survey frequency limited.
Coastal Deeh (SO08) Bari district; structural fishing/pastoral mix with moderate vulnerability. Remote location reduces survey frequency.
Bari urban-pastoral district within Puntland with consistent administrative access. Some IDP hosting; reliable CMAM and surveys.

Puntland state capital with the most consistent administrative access in northeast Somalia. Garowe IDPs have shown sustained Critical/Serious GAM, raising gamma; survey infrastructure excellent (very low omega); CMAM strong.
Coastal Deeh (SO08) Nugaal district; structural pastoral/fishing mix. Puntland administrative access supports moderate CMAM; remote rural surveys irregular.
Addun Pastoral (SO09) Nugaal district. Stable Puntland administration supports moderate CMAM and surveys; pastoral vulnerability gives moderate structural risk.
Sool regional capital in contested Somaliland/Puntland zone; Hawd Pastoral hinterland. Periodic political tension limits programme stability; otherwise structurally moderate.
Hawd Pastoral (SO05) Sool district; remote pastoral economy with limited service infrastructure. Survey frequency low raising omega.
Sool pastoral district, remote with limited service coverage. Hawd-Northern Inland pastoral mix; structurally moderate, omega elevated by sparse surveys.
Mixed Hawd Pastoral and Northwest Agropastoral district; relatively stable Somaliland administrative access. Moderate structural vulnerability.
Sanaag regional capital in Northern Inland Pastoral (SO06); Somaliland-administered with moderate CMAM access. Some IDP hosting; structurally moderate vulnerability.
Sanaag district mixing Northern Inland Pastoral and West Golis livelihoods. Stable Somaliland administration with moderate CMAM presence.
Coastal Sanaag district mixing East Golis and Northern Inland Pastoral. Remote, intermittent CMAM access; surveys infrequent raise omega.

Togdheer regional capital, second-largest urban centre in Somaliland; reliable administration supports CMAM and FSNAU surveys (low omega). Some IDP hosting; structural agropastoral/pastoral hinterland of moderate vulnerability.
Togdheer/Sool border Hawd Pastoral district. Stable administration; structurally pastoral with moderate vulnerability.
Togdheer Agropastoral (SO04) district. Diversified rural economy; stable Somaliland administration; moderate CMAM.
Togdheer highlands district within West Golis Pastoral (SO02). Highland pastoral diversification supports relatively low structural vulnerability.

Somaliland capital; the country's most stable urban environment with strong public services, diversified economy, and consistent FSNAU survey infrastructure (very low omega). IDP hosting elevates gamma slightly; structural risk lowest tier.
Somaliland port city bordering Guban Pastoral (SO01) which has historically shown Critical SAM. Urban core lowers risk, but coastal Guban hinterland keeps structural vulnerability moderate.
Northwest Agropastoral (SO03) district in Somaliland; among most diversified rural economies with reliable surveys and CMAM. Low structural vulnerability.
Awdal regional capital; West Golis/NW Agropastoral mix. Stable administration, diversified livelihoods, reliable CMAM and surveys; relatively low structural risk.
Awdal district at the boundary of Guban Pastoral (SO01, historically Critical SAM) and West Golis. Coastal pastoral pressure raises structural vulnerability; moderate CMAM.

Coastal Guban Pastoral (SO01) district; Guban has historically been one of the few zones with Critical SAM (>4%) in FSNAU surveys despite Somaliland administration. Hot, arid, structurally vulnerable; remote with sparse surveys.
Coastal Guban Pastoral (SO01) district along the Djibouti border; historically Critical SAM. Structurally hot/arid pastoral economy with chronic vulnerability and irregular surveys.
